title: Chapter 136 — Online Reviews & Reputation
intro: One bad Google review can cost you more than a hundred good sales days.

sections.title: Responding to Negative Reviews
sections.content:
Never get defensive. Never argue. Never blame the customer. The potential customers reading your response are evaluating how you handle problems.

Template: 'Thank you for sharing your experience, [name]. I am sorry we did not meet your expectations. I would like to make this right — please call me directly at [number] so I can help.' Take it offline. Resolve it privately. Then the customer often updates or removes the review.

sections.title: Building a Review Culture
sections.content:
Do not wait for reviews to happen organically. Build a system. Ask every satisfied customer at the right moment — 48 hours to one week after delivery. Send the direct link. Make it one click.

The math of reviews: a store with 50 five-star reviews and one 1-star review has a 4.9 rating. A store with 5 five-star reviews and one 1-star review has a 4.2 rating. Volume protects you. Build the volume proactively.

sections.title: What Never to Say Publicly
sections.content:
Never disclose customer details in a public response. Never admit liability or fault in writing. Never promise specific compensation publicly. Never argue with the reviewer.

Keep public responses short, empathetic, and focused on moving the conversation offline. Everything you write is permanent and visible to every future customer.
